claim: In M71 transgenic mice, more than 95% of all olfactory sensory neurons express a single odorant receptor, M71.
source: In these mice, more than 95% of all olfactory sensory neurons express a single odorant receptor, M71.
evidence: Direct statement in the abstract describing the genetic manipulation in M71 transgenic mice.

claim: The frequency of sensory neurons expressing endogenous odorant receptor genes is reduced 20-fold in M71 transgenic mice.
source: As a consequence of this genetic manipulation, the frequency of sensory neurons expressing endogenous odorant receptor genes is reduced 20-fold, and the canonical glomerular odor map observed in wild-type mice disappears
evidence: Statement in the introduction describing the consequence of M71 overexpression on endogenous receptor expression.

claim: Most odorants fail to elicit detectable levels of glomerular activity in M71 transgenic mice.
source: most odorants now fail to elicit detectable levels of glomerular activity, while the majority of glomeruli respond to acetophenone, a known M71 ligand (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statement supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing altered glomerular activity patterns.

claim: M71 transgenic mice can detect and discriminate several odorants in a go/no go operant conditioning task.
source: Surprisingly, despite this striking alteration of odor-evoked neural activity, M71 transgenic mice are able to smell a variety of odors. They can detect and discriminate several odorants in a go/no go operant conditioning task
evidence: Behavioral observation reported in the introduction describing preserved olfactory discrimination abilities.

claim: M71 transgenic mice fail to discriminate acetophenone from air in a go/no go discrimination assay.
source: Moreover, M71 transgenic mice fail to discriminate acetophenone, a known strong M71 ligand, from air in this go/no go discrimination assay, despite the fact that acetophenone activates the vast majority of sensory neurons and glomeruli in these mice.
evidence: Behavioral finding reported in the introduction describing a specific deficit in acetophenone discrimination.

claim: Mitral cell odor responses in M71 transgenic mice greatly resemble the responses observed in wild-type mice.
source: Two-photon calcium imaging and whole cell patch-clamp recordings of mitral cells revealed that mitral cell odor responses in M71 transgenic mice greatly resembled the responses observed in wild-type mice.
evidence: Summary statement in the introduction describing the main finding from calcium imaging and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: The fraction of responsive mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice is indistinguishable from controls.
source: Indeed, the fraction of responsive mitral cells and odor-evoked changes in firing rates were indistinguishable from controls.
evidence: Quantitative comparison of mitral cell responses between M71 transgenic and control mice reported in the introduction.

claim: Odor-evoked changes in firing rates of mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice are indistinguishable from controls.
source: Indeed, the fraction of responsive mitral cells and odor-evoked changes in firing rates were indistinguishable from controls.
evidence: Quantitative comparison of mitral cell firing rate changes between M71 transgenic and control mice.

claim: Normalization of odor-evoked activity in M71 transgenic mice is achieved through inhibition by periglomerular interneurons.
source: Calcium imaging and whole cell recordings further indicated that much of this normalization of odor-evoked activity is achieved through inhibition by periglomerular interneurons.
evidence: Mechanistic conclusion from calcium imaging and electrophysiology experiments reported in the introduction.

claim: M71 transgenic mice exhibit spontaneous sniff adaptation in response to acetophenone exposure.
source: Finally, we found that M71 transgenic mice exhibit spontaneous sniff adaptation in response to acetophenone exposure, suggesting that while they consistently fail to discriminate acetophenone from air in a go/no-go operant conditioning tasks they are indeed able to detect the presence of acetophenone.
evidence: Behavioral finding from sniff adaptation experiments reported in the introduction.

claim: M71 transgenic mice consistently failed to discriminate acetophenone from mineral oil in a go/no go operant conditioning task.
source: Consistent with our initial observations, we found that M71 transgenic mice consistently failed to detect acteophenone in this task (acetophenone versus mineral oil, repeated measure ANOVA, (block x genotype) F(9,90) = 5.43, p<0.001)
evidence: Statistical result from behavioral experiments comparing acetophenone discrimination between genotypes.

claim: M71 transgenic mice readily discriminated ethyl acetate from mineral oil, citronellol, or carvone.
source: yet readily discriminated other pairs of odorants (ethyl acetate versus mineral oil, citronellol, or carvone, (block x genotype) F(9,90) = 1.49, p=0.17, Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Statistical result from behavioral experiments showing preserved discrimination of non-acetophenone odorants.

claim: All 15 M71 transgenic mice tested failed to reach a 'correct lick ratio' surpassing 75% for acetophenone discrimination.
source: Individual experiments consisted of 10 blocks of 20 odor presentations, and all 15 M71 transgenic mice failed to reach a 'correct lick ratio' surpassing 75%.
evidence: Quantitative behavioral result describing the consistent failure of M71 transgenic mice in acetophenone discrimination.

claim: All 15 M71 transgenic mice successfully discriminated ethyl acetate from mineral oil, citronellol, or carvone.
source: In contrast, the same 15 M71 transgenic mice all successfully discriminated ethyl acetate from mineral oil, citronellol, or carvone (Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Behavioral result showing preserved discrimination ability for non-acetophenone odorants.

claim: Wild-type mice exhibited increased sniff frequencies when exposed to a novel odorant.
source: As previously described, wild-type mice exhibited increased sniff frequencies when exposed to a novel odorant (mean response = 2.1 Hz, SD = 1.6 Hz)
evidence: Quantitative behavioral observation from sniff adaptation experiments in control mice.

claim: Wild-type mice showed decreased sniff frequencies upon repeated presentation of the same odorant.
source: that then decreased upon repeated presentation of the same odorant (mean response for 2nd and 3rd presentation = 0.3 Hz, SD = 1.2 Hz, p=3.3 x10-7, paired t-test 1st presentation versus mean of 2nd and 3rd, n = 27 mouse-odor pairs, n = 7 mice, Figure 1C–F).
evidence: Statistical result from sniff adaptation experiments showing habituation in control mice.

claim: M71 transgenic mice exhibited an initial increase in sniff frequency to non-acetophenone odors that was indistinguishable from controls.
source: Consistent with their ability to detect and discriminate most odorants, M71 transgenic mice exhibited an initial increase in sniff frequency to ethyl acetate, hexanone, heptanal, or a mixture of isoamyl acetate, 2-nonanone and cyclohexanol (referred to as 'non-acetophenone' odors in Figure 1F, mean response = 2.7 Hz, SD = 1.4 Hz). This response was indistinguishable from controls (p=0.12, t-test)
evidence: Statistical comparison of sniff responses to non-acetophenone odors between M71 transgenic and control mice.

claim: M71 transgenic mice displayed a significant decrease in sniff frequencies upon re-exposure to non-acetophenone odors.
source: and similarly displayed a significant decrease in sniff frequencies upon re-exposure (p=1.7 x 10–8, paired t-test, n = 29 mouse-odor pairs, n = 8 mice, Figure 1G).
evidence: Statistical result showing sniff habituation to non-acetophenone odors in M71 transgenic mice.

claim: Both control and M71 transgenic mice displayed initial high frequency sniff responses to acetophenone.
source: Surprisingly, similar results were obtained for acetophenone presentations: both control and M71 transgenic mice displayed initial high frequency responses (control: mean = 3.0 Hz, SD = 1.6 Hz; M71 transgenic: mean = 3.8 Hz, SD = 1.9 Hz, p=0.38, t-test)
evidence: Statistical comparison of initial sniff responses to acetophenone between genotypes.

claim: Both control and M71 transgenic mice showed reductions in sniff response frequencies during the second and third acetophenone presentation.
source: and reductions in response frequencies during the second and third acetophenone presentation (Figure 1F and G, right panels).
evidence: Observation of sniff habituation to acetophenone in both genotypes supported by figure reference.

claim: M71 transgenic mice can identify acetophenone in a spontaneous test for odor detection.
source: Together, these results indicate that in contrast to the aforementioned go/no go operant conditioning task, M71 transgenic mice can identify acetophenone in a spontaneous test for odor detection.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from sniff adaptation experiments showing task-dependent acetophenone detection.

claim: Rabies virus-mediated expression of GCaMP3 permits the visualization of odor-evoked responses specifically in mitral cells.
source: We developed an in vivo imaging approach that permits the visualization of odor-evoked responses specifically in mitral cells, the main output neurons of the olfactory bulb. We used a replication-deficient recombinant rabies virus to drive the expression of the calcium-sensitive indicator of neural activity GCaMP3 (RVΔG-4GCaMP3) (Tian et al., 2009; Wickersham et al., 2010) in large populations of mitral cells.
evidence: Description of the imaging method with citations to supporting literature.

claim: The modified rabies virus is unable to spread transsynaptically, restricting GCaMP3 expression to neurons directly infected via their axonal terminations.
source: Because this modified rabies virus lacks the gene encoding its viral glycoprotein, it is unable to spread transsynaptically, thereby restricting the expression of GCaMP3 to neurons directly infected via their axonal terminations (Wickersham et al., 2007; 2010).
evidence: Explanation of viral specificity mechanism with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Infected cells began to exhibit clear signs of toxicity after 12 days post-infection.
source: However, because the virus retains its ability to replicate in infected cells, we found that infected cells began exhibit clear signs of toxicity after 12 days (not shown).
evidence: Observation of viral toxicity limiting the experimental time window.

claim: All imaging experiments were performed within 5–7 days after virus injections.
source: We therefore performed all imaging experiments within 5–7 days after virus injections.
evidence: Methodological detail describing the timing of experiments to avoid viral toxicity.

claim: GCaMP3-expressing mitral cells were uniformly distributed across the olfactory bulb.
source: Using this method, we were able to selectively express GCaMP3 in hundreds of mitral cells in the olfactory bulb (Figure 2B–D). GCaMP3-expressing mitral cells were uniformly distributed across the olfactory bulb.
evidence: Observation from imaging experiments describing the spatial distribution of labeled cells.

claim: The cell bodies of GCaMP3-expressing neurons were exclusively located in the mitral cell layer.
source: The cell bodies of GCaMP3-expressing neurons were exclusively located in the mitral cell layer, and we often observed multiple GCaMP3-expressing mitral cells projecting to the same glomerulus (Figure 2C).
evidence: Anatomical observation confirming cell-type specificity of the labeling method.

claim: Rabies-GCaMP3 virus permits the highly efficient and selective labeling of mitral cells projecting to the piriform cortex.
source: While we cannot exclude the possibility that GCaMP3 is also expressed in some tufted cells, these results demonstrate that rabies-GCaMP3 virus permits the highly efficient and selective labeling of mitral cells projecting to the piriform cortex.
evidence: Conclusion about the specificity of the labeling method with acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: Odorants at low concentrations (0.01%) typically evoked sparse, spatially distributed patterns of activity in ~15% of mitral cells in wild-type mice.
source: In wild-type mice, we found that odorants at low concentrations (0.01%, or 1/10,000 vol./vol. dilution) typically evoked sparse, spatially distributed patterns of activity in ~15% of mitral cells (mean = 14.5%, standard deviation (SD) = 11.2%; Figure 2F and H).
evidence: Quantitative result from calcium imaging experiments in control mice.

claim: The calcium imaging observations are consistent with recent results using AAV-mediated and transgenic GCaMP3 expression.
source: These observations are consistent with recent results using adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated and transgenic GCaMP3 expression (Blauvelt et al., 2013; Kato et al., 2012; Wachowiak et al., 2013).
evidence: Comparison of current findings with published literature to establish consistency.

claim: Mitral cells responsive to a given odorant were typically distributed across the imaging site and did not exhibit segregated patterns.
source: Furthermore, mitral cells responsive to a given odorant were typically distributed across the imaging site and did not exhibit the segregated patterns observed in odor-evoked glomerular activity.
evidence: Observation about the spatial organization of odor-responsive mitral cells.

claim: The fraction and distribution of odor-responsive mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice and their wild-type littermate controls were strikingly similar.
source: We next performed these same imaging experiments using M71 transgenic mice. Remarkably, we found that the fraction and distribution of odor-responsive mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice and their wild-type littermate controls were strikingly similar (Figure 2I).
evidence: Comparative observation from calcium imaging experiments between genotypes.

claim: Ethyl acetate and eugenol do not activate M71-expressing olfactory sensory neurons at all concentrations tested.
source: Ethyl acetate or eugenol, for example, do not activate M71-expressing olfactory sensory neurons at all concentrations tested (Bozza et al., 2002)
evidence: Statement about receptor-ligand interactions supported by citation to published work.

claim: Ethyl acetate and eugenol do not elicit detectable glomerular activity in M71 transgenic mice.
source: and do not elicit detectable glomerular activity in M71 transgenic mice (Fleischmann et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement about glomerular responses supported by citation to previous work.

claim: All test odorants including ethyl acetate and eugenol evoked mitral cell responses in M71 transgenic mice.
source: However, we found that all test odorants including ethyl acetate and eugenol evoked mitral cell responses.
evidence: Observation from calcium imaging showing responses to odorants that don't activate M71 receptor.

claim: The fractions of odor-responsive neurons in M71 transgenic mice were indistinguishable from wild-type littermate controls.
source: Moreover, the fractions of odor-responsive neurons were indistinguishable from wild-type littermate controls (mixed-effect ANOVA (genotype x odorants), F(13, 242) = 0.58, p=0.87, Figure 2H and I).
evidence: Statistical comparison of mitral cell response fractions between genotypes.

claim: Acetophenone is a known strong M71 receptor ligand.
source: Given that 95% of all olfactory sensory neurons in these mice express the M71 receptor, we next examined mitral cell responses to acetophenone, a known strong M71 receptor ligand (Bozza et al., 2002)
evidence: Statement about receptor-ligand interaction supported by citation.

claim: Acetophenone evoked pervasive glomerular activation of the dorsal surface of the olfactory bulb in M71 transgenic mice.
source: that evoked pervasive glomerular activation of the dorsal surface of the olfactory bulb of M71 transgenic mice (Fleischmann et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement about glomerular responses to acetophenone supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The fraction of mitral cells activated by acetophenone was virtually identical to littermate controls.
source: We observed two surprising findings: first, the fraction of mitral cells activated by acetophenone was virtually identical to littermate controls
evidence: Comparative observation from calcium imaging experiments for acetophenone responses.

claim: The fraction of mitral cells responding to acetophenone was highly similar to the fractions of mitral cells responding to other odorants.
source: and second, the fraction of mitral cells responding to acetophenone was highly similar to the fractions of mitral cells responding to other odorants (Figure 2H,I right).
evidence: Comparative observation showing similar response fractions across different odorants.

claim: The OB circuitry profoundly normalizes activity, strengthening weakened input from odorants that do not activate the M71 receptor.
source: Given the massively altered glomerular input and essentially normal mitral cell output, these imaging data indicate that the OB circuitry profoundly normalizes activity, strengthening the weakened input from odorants that do not activate the M71 receptor
evidence: Interpretive conclusion drawn from the comparison of glomerular input and mitral cell output.

claim: The OB circuitry suppresses the overt excitation due to the M71 ligand acetophenone.
source: and suppressing the overt excitation due to the M71 ligand acetophenone, resulting in responses that – on the crude level of overall activation – were indistinguishable from wild-type mice.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about signal suppression mechanism inferred from imaging data.

claim: Individual mitral cells in controls generally displayed narrow stimulus tuning at low odor concentrations.
source: In controls, individual mitral cells generally displayed narrow stimulus tuning at low odor concentrations, in accord with previously published results from electrophysiological and optical recordings (Figure 3A) (Davison and Katz, 2007; Kato et al., 2012; Tan et al., 2010).
evidence: Observation about mitral cell tuning properties supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Approximately 46.1% of mitral cells in controls did not respond to any of the 13 odorants in the stimulus set.
source: Approximately half of the neurons (46.1%) did not respond to any of the 13 odorants in the stimulus set used to probe selectivity
evidence: Quantitative result from calcium imaging describing the fraction of non-responsive neurons.

claim: The majority of odor-responsive neurons (43.9% of all neurons) displayed significant increases in fluorescence to only 1–5 odor stimuli.
source: while the majority of odor-responsive neurons (43.9% of all neurons) displayed significant increases in fluorescence to only 1–5 odor stimuli.
evidence: Quantitative result describing the tuning breadth of responsive mitral cells.

claim: A small subpopulation (10.0%) of mitral cells were more broadly tuned.
source: A small subpopulation (10.0%) of mitral cells were more broadly tuned.
evidence: Quantitative result describing the fraction of broadly tuned mitral cells.

claim: The majority of stimulus-evoked mitral cell response magnitudes were small, with peak ΔF/F values below 35%.
source: Moreover, the majority of stimulus-evoked mitral cell response magnitudes were small, with peak ΔF/F values below 35%, although we could observe a small number of large stimulus-evoked responses with ΔF/F values of up to 200% (Figure 3C).
evidence: Quantitative description of response magnitude distribution from calcium imaging.

claim: The fluorescence levels of most odor-responsive neurons (>80%) returned to baseline within 8 s after response onset.
source: Finally, the fluorescence levels of most odor-responsive neurons (>80%) returned to baseline within 8 s after response onset (Figure 3D).
evidence: Quantitative result describing response duration from calcium imaging.

claim: Mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice tended to be more broadly tuned than controls, but this difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: In M71 transgenic mice, mitral cells tended to be more broadly tuned (Figure 3A and B), but this difference did not reach statistical significance (Chi-squared test: χ2 = 17.7, p=0.17).
evidence: Statistical comparison of tuning breadth between genotypes.

claim: The distribution of response magnitudes of mitral cells in M71 transgenic mice was shifted towards smaller peak ΔF/F values.
source: For acetophenone and the 12 other odorants, the distribution of the response magnitudes of mitral cell was shifted towards smaller peak ΔF/F values, with a particularly large reduction in the number of strongly responding neurons (i.e. those reaching ΔF/F values of greater than 50%; Figure 3C, median ΔF/F: control: 0.36, M71 transgenic: 0.32; mean ΔF/F: control: 0.47, M71 transgenic: 0.38, Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: D4116,1639 = 0.12, p<0.01, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statistical comparison of response magnitude distributions between genotypes.

claim: The average response duration of M71 transgenic mitral cells to acetophenone and the 12 other odorants was significantly increased.
source: In contrast, the average response duration of M71 transgenic mitral cells to acetophenone and the 12 other odorants was significantly increased (Figure 3D, Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: D4116,1639 = 0.24, p<0.01, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statistical comparison of response durations between genotypes.

claim: The fraction of neurons responding on all 4 out of 4 repeat presentations of the same odorant was reduced from 14% in controls to 2.9% in M71 transgenic mice.
source: In M71 transgenic mice, the fraction of neurons responding on all 4 out of 4 repeat presentations of the same odorant was reduced from 14% in controls to 2.9% in M71 transgenic mice.
evidence: Quantitative comparison of response reliability between genotypes.

claim: The mean correlation of response patterns to individual exposures of the same odorant was reduced in M71 transgenic mice compared to controls.
source: Furthermore, we calculated the Pearson correlation coefficients of the activity patterns after odor onset. We found that for acetophenone and the 12 other odorants, the mean correlation of response patterns to individual exposures of the same odorant was reduced in M71 transgenic mice compared to controls (controls: mean across 13 odorants = 0.75 ± 0.11; M71: mean = 0.25 ± 0.17, Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Statistical comparison of trial-to-trial variability between genotypes using correlation analysis.

claim: The biophysical properties of MTCs were, on average, similar in M71 transgenic mice and controls.
source: First, we characterized the intrinsic properties of MTCs, including resting membrane potentials, input resistance, membrane time constant tau, and baseline firing rates. These biophysical properties of MTCs were, on average, similar in M71 transgenic mice (n = 6 cells from 6 mice) and controls (n = 7 cells from 5 mice, Figure 4A–G).
evidence: Comparative analysis of electrophysiological properties from whole-cell recordings.

claim: MTCs in M71 transgenic mice appeared to be less heterogeneous compared to wild-type for baseline firing rate.
source: Interestingly, however, we observed that MTCs in M71 transgenic mice appeared to be less heterogeneous compared to wild-type, in particular for baseline firing rate (Control: 5.8 ± 6.2 Hz, M71: 3.0 ± 1.0 Hz, p=0.003 Bartlett test)
evidence: Statistical comparison of variance in baseline firing rates between genotypes.

claim: MTCs in M71 transgenic mice appeared to be less heterogeneous compared to wild-type for theta modulation strength.
source: and theta modulation strength (Control: 0.4 ± 0.4 mV, M71: 0.2 ± 0.1 mV, p=0.01 Bartlett test)
evidence: Statistical comparison of variance in theta modulation between genotypes.

claim: The reduced heterogeneity in M71 transgenic MTCs might reflect their more homogeneous olfactory inputs and developmental history.
source: which might reflect their more homogeneous olfactory inputs and thus developmental history (Angelo et al., 2012).
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the reduced heterogeneity with citation to supporting literature.

claim: Mean changes in firing rate to non-acetophenone odors were indistinguishable between M71 transgenic mice and controls.
source: Consistent with our imaging data, we found that overall firing rate distributions to the same 4 stimuli were more compact in M71 transgenic mice; mean changes in firing rate were indistinguishable from controls (mean Δ firing rateM71 = 0.75 Hz, SD = 2.2 Hz, 20 cell/odor pairs, p=0.67, Rank-sum, Figure 4M)
evidence: Statistical comparison of firing rate changes from whole-cell recordings.

claim: The fraction of excitatory responses to non-acetophenone odors was similar between M71 transgenic mice and controls.
source: yet the fraction of excitatory responses was similar (control: 32%, M71: 25%).
evidence: Quantitative comparison of response types from whole-cell recordings.

claim: Both excitatory and inhibitory responses to non-acetophenone odors were generally weaker in M71 transgenic mice.
source: However, both excitatory and inhibitory responses were generally weaker (Δ|Vm|M71 = 0.5+[-0.3 0.8] mV, Δ|Vm|cntrl = 1.3+[-0.6 2.5] mV, p=0.006, Wilcoxon rank sum; Δ |firing rate|M71 = 0.8+[-0.3 1.6]yy Hz, Δ|firing rate|cntrl = 6.0+[-3.0 6.2] Hz, p<0.001, Wilcoxon rank sum, median +[lower quartile, upper quartile])
evidence: Statistical comparison of response magnitudes from whole-cell recordings.

claim: Strong excitatory responses were notably absent in M71 transgenic mice.
source: and strong excitatory responses notably absent in M71 transgenic mice (Figure 4M).
evidence: Observation from whole-cell recordings about the absence of strong excitatory responses.

claim: Inhibitory responses to non-acetophenone odors were substantially reduced in M71 transgenic mice compared to littermate controls.
source: Most prominently, inhibitory responses were substantially reduced compared to littermate controls (p=0.003, Rank-sum, Figure 4L).
evidence: Statistical comparison of inhibitory responses from whole-cell recordings.

claim: In M71 transgenic mice, acetophenone exposure caused a massive and prolonged increase in theta modulation of the membrane potential.
source: Strikingly, in M71 transgenic mice, acetophenone exposure caused a massive and prolonged increase in theta modulation of the membrane potential (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Observation from whole-cell recordings showing increased theta oscillations in response to acetophenone.

claim: Mean firing rate change induced by acetophenone was not significantly different between M71 transgenic mice and controls.
source: Phasic odor responses, however, were highly similar in control and M71 transgenic mice: mean firing rate change induced by acetophenone was again not significantly different between M71 transgenic mice and controls (control: -0.2 ± 7.5 Hz, M71: -0.5 ± 2.7 Hz, p=0.89, t-test, Figure 5F and H)
evidence: Statistical comparison of acetophenone-evoked firing rate changes from whole-cell recordings.

claim: Acetophenone generally induced prolonged hyperpolarizations in M71 transgenic mice, whereas responses were more transient in littermate controls.
source: However, acetophenone generally induced prolonged hyperpolarizations in M71 transgenic mice, whereas responses were more transient in littermate controls (responses over 5 s window: control: -0.7 ± 0.5 mV, M71: -2.2 ± 1.9 mV, p<0.05, 1-tailed t-test. Figure 5E,G and I, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statistical comparison of acetophenone-evoked membrane potential responses from whole-cell recordings.

claim: Feedforward inhibition from olfactory bulb periglomerular cells can mediate signal normalization in M71 transgenic mice.
source: In vivo whole cell recordings suggest that feedforward inhibition from olfactory bulb periglomerular cells can mediate this signal normalization.
evidence: Mechanistic conclusion from whole-cell recordings reported in the abstract.

claim: Slow, odor-evoked phasic inhibition likely originates in the glomerular layer.
source: Previous work indicated that such slow, odor-evoked phasic inhibition likely originates in the glomerular layer (Fukunaga et al., 2014)
evidence: Statement about the source of inhibition supported by citation to published work.

claim: In control mice, only a fraction of PG cells displayed responses to either acetophenone or ethyl acetate (acetophenone: 10.9%; ethyl acetate: 12.1%).
source: In control mice, only a fraction of PG cells displayed responses to either acetophenone or ethyl acetate (acetophenone: 10.9%; ethyl acetate: 12.1%, Figure 5O and Figure 6G).
evidence: Quantitative result from PG cell calcium imaging in control mice.

claim: The magnitudes of odor-evoked PG cell responses in controls were small, with more than 80% of peak ∆F/F values below 10%.
source: The magnitudes of these odor-evoked responses were small, with more than 80% of peak ∆F/F values below 10% (data not shown).
evidence: Quantitative description of PG cell response magnitudes in controls.

claim: Exposure of M71 transgenic mice to acetophenone at 0.01% resulted in pervasive, strong and persistent activity in over 48% of PG cells, significantly higher than in littermate controls.
source: Exposure of M71 transgenic mice to acetophenone, even at the lowest concentration (0.01% vol./vol.), resulted in pervasive, strong and persistent activity in over 48% of PG cells, significantly higher than in littermate controls (Figure 5P and Figure 6H, Rank-sum test nco = 10, nM71 transgenic = 9, U = 83, p<0.01).
evidence: Statistical comparison of acetophenone-evoked PG cell responses between genotypes.

claim: The magnitude and duration of acetophenone-evoked PG cell activity was significantly increased in M71 transgenic mice compared to controls.
source: Furthermore, the magnitude and duration of acetophenone-evoked PG cell activity was significantly increased in M71 transgenic mice compared to controls (data not shown).
evidence: Comparative observation of PG cell response properties between genotypes.

claim: Ethyl acetate elicited PG cell activity in only a small population of neurons (<10%) in M71 transgenic mice.
source: In contrast to these robust and pervasive responses to acetophenone, ethyl acetate elicited PG cell activity in only a small population of neurons (<10%, Figure 5P and Figure 6H)
evidence: Quantitative result from PG cell calcium imaging showing sparse responses to ethyl acetate.

claim: Pervasive and strong glomerular excitation is balanced by similarly pervasive and strong periglomerular inhibition to normalize olfactory bulb mitral cell output.
source: Taken together, electrophysiology and imaging experiments indicate that pervasive and strong glomerular excitation is balanced by similarly pervasive and strong periglomerular inhibition to normalize olfactory bulb mitral cell output.
evidence: Integrative conclusion drawn from electrophysiology and imaging experiments.

claim: In control mice, a 10- and 100-fold increase in acetophenone or ethyl acetate concentration only caused a modest increase in mitral cell activity.
source: In control mice, a 10- and 100-fold increase in acetophenone or ethyl acetate concentration only caused a modest increase in mitral cell activity: about 15% of mitral cells responded to either odorant at 0.1% dilutions, and ~20% of mitral cells responded at 1% dilutions (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: Quantitative result from concentration series imaging experiments in controls.

claim: Increasing concentrations of acetophenone in M71 transgenic mice dramatically increased the fraction of responsive mitral cells.
source: In marked contrast to controls, increasing concentrations of acetophenone in M71 transgenic mice dramatically increased the fraction of responsive mitral cells: acetophenone at 0.1% activated over 28% of mitral cells (mean = 28.7% ± 17.1%), while over 50% (mean = 50.1% ± 25.8%) of mitral cells responded at 1% acetophenone (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: Quantitative result showing concentration-dependent increase in mitral cell responses to acetophenone.

claim: The number of responsive neurons was highly correlated to acetophenone concentration in M71 transgenic mice.
source: The number of responsive neurons was highly correlated to acetophenone concentration (n = 10, Pearson's correlation coefficient = 0.71)
evidence: Statistical analysis showing correlation between acetophenone concentration and response density.

claim: Response magnitudes sharply increased with increasing acetophenone concentrations in M71 transgenic mice, but response durations were reduced.
source: Furthermore, although response magnitudes sharply increased with increasing acetophenone concentrations, response durations were reduced (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Observation of concentration-dependent changes in response properties.

claim: The striking sensitivity to acetophenone concentration was not observed for ethyl acetate in M71 transgenic mice.
source: The striking sensitivity to acetophenone concentration was not observed for ethyl acetate. A ten-fold increase in ethyl acetate concentration resulted in only a ~1.5-fold increase in the fraction of responsive mitral cells, and a hungred-fold increase in ethyl acetate activated ~2 times more cells, essentially identical to what we observed in controls (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: Comparative observation showing stimulus-specific concentration dependence.

claim: Increasing acetophenone concentrations dramatically increased PG cell activity in M71 transgenic mice.
source: While PG cells were already quite responsive to low acetophenone concentrations in M71 transgenic mice, increasing acetophenone concentrations dramatically increased PG cell activity in these mice (Figure 6F and H): 0.1% activated over 85% (mean 85.1% ± 13%) of PG cells in M71 transgenic mice compared to only 10.8% ( ± 6.6%) observed in controls.
evidence: Quantitative result showing concentration-dependent increase in PG cell responses.

claim: A further ten-fold increase in acetophenone concentration (1%) increased the fraction of responsive PG cells to 94% in M71 transgenic mice.
source: A further ten-fold increase in concentration (1%) increased the fraction of responsive neurons to 94% ( ± 8%) in M71 transgenic mice.
evidence: Quantitative result showing near-saturation of PG cell responses at high acetophenone concentrations.

claim: At high acetophenone concentrations, periglomerular inhibition fails to counterbalance excitation in M71 transgenic mice.
source: These data therefore suggest that at high acetophenone concentrations, periglomerular inhibition fails to counterbalance excitation.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the breakdown of normalization at high concentrations.

claim: Ethyl acetate may be a weak M71 receptor agonist that activates M71 at high concentrations.
source: Although ethyl acetate has previously been reported not to activate the M71 receptor (Bozza et al., 2002), these data suggest that ethyl acetate may in fact be a weak M71 receptor agonist that activates M71 at high concentrations.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of PG cell responses to high concentrations of ethyl acetate.

claim: PG cell responses to both acetophenone and ethyl acetate were pervasive and not restricted to individual glomeruli in M71 transgenic mice.
source: This speculation is supported by the observation that while odorants activate segregated, glomerulus-specific clusters of PG cells in wild-type mice, PG cell responses to both acetophenone and ethyl acetate were pervasive and not restricted to individual glomeruli in M71 transgenic mice, consistent with the pervasive glomerular innervation by M71-expressing sensory inputs (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: Observation about the spatial organization of PG cell responses supporting the speculation about ethyl acetate.

claim: Calcium imaging experiments reveal that olfactory bulb mitral cell output in M71 transgenic mice is surprisingly similar to that observed in wild-type mice.
source: We have characterized the transformation of odor-evoked activity in the olfactory bulb of M71 transgenic mice with a 'monoclonal nose', in which glomerular input patterns are massively perturbed. Calcium imaging experiments reveal that olfactory bulb mitral cell output in M71 transgenic mice is surprisingly similar to that observed wild-type mice.
evidence: Summary statement in the discussion synthesizing the main finding from imaging experiments.

claim: Cell-specific calcium imaging together with in vivo patch-clamp recordings identify feedforward periglomerular inhibition as a major candidate neural circuit mechanism for signal amplification and suppression.
source: Cell-specific calcium imaging together with in vivo patch-clamp recordings identify feedforward periglomerular inhibition as a major candidate neural circuit mechanism for signal amplification and suppression.
evidence: Summary statement in the discussion identifying the mechanistic basis for normalization.

claim: The olfactory bulb has a remarkable capacity to extract meaningful information from degraded sensory input.
source: Our results thus highlight the capacity of the olfactory bulb to extract meaningful information from degraded sensory input.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the functional significance of the findings.

claim: Acetophenone-evoked suprathreshold mitral cell activity in M71 transgenic mice is surprisingly similar to that observed in wild-type mice.
source: However, our calcium imaging and electrophysiological recordings do not support this hypothesis. Instead, we observe that acetophenone-evoked suprathreshold mitral cell activity in M71 transgenic mice is surprisingly similar to that observed in wild-type mice: the fraction of acetophenone-responsive neurons, and acetophenone-induced changes in mitral cell firing rates are indistinguishable from controls.
evidence: Summary of findings contradicting a previous hypothesis about acetophenone detection failure.

claim: A single one second puff of acetophenone elicits strong theta oscillations that last for at least 20 s in M71 transgenic mice.
source: The most striking acetophenone-specific effect we observe is a massive amplification of theta oscillations. A single one second puff of acetophenone elicits strong theta oscillations that last for at least 20 s.
evidence: Observation from electrophysiology experiments describing prolonged oscillatory activity.

claim: Prolonged network perturbations may interfere with the discrimination of acetophenone from clean air in the go/no go operant conditioning task.
source: The behavioral consequences of this oscillatory activity are unknown, but it is possible that these prolonged network perturbations interfere with the discrimination of acetophenone from clean air in the go/no go operant conditioning task.
evidence: Speculative interpretation about the behavioral consequences of prolonged theta oscillations.

claim: Strong oscillatory network activity may precede an epileptic state, which could obstruct odor discrimination.
source: Finally, strong oscillatory network activity may precede an epileptic state (Nguyen and Ryba, 2012), which could obstruct odor discrimination.
evidence: Speculative interpretation with citation suggesting a possible mechanism for behavioral deficit.

claim: Spontaneous sniff adaptation does not require that mice accurately discriminate between successive presentations of two different stimuli.
source: Spontaneous sniff adaptation does not require that mice accurately discriminate between successive presentations of two different stimuli.
evidence: Statement about the cognitive demands of the sniff adaptation task.

claim: The heightened level of anxiety in M71 transgenic mice might amplify sniff responses to novel stimuli including to non-olfactory components of the stimulus.
source: Additionally, the heightened level of anxiety in M71 transgenic mice (Glinka et al., 2012) might amplify sniff responses to novel stimuli including to non-olfactory components of the stimulus.
evidence: Speculative interpretation with citation about potential confounds in sniff behavior.

claim: Training in operant conditioning may shape the processing of odor-evoked activity, and such plastic changes may underlie the task dependency of the behavioral deficit.
source: It is possible that training, which is performed with non-acetophenone odorants, may shape the processing of odor-evoked activity, and that such plastic changes may underlie the task dependency of the behavioral deficit.
evidence: Speculative interpretation about the role of learning in task-dependent behavior.

claim: PG cells are pervasively and robustly activated by acetophenone in M71 transgenic mice.
source: We now show that PG cells are pervasively and robustly activated by acetophenone in M71 transgenic mice.
evidence: Summary of PG cell imaging findings in the discussion.

claim: Acetophenone evokes strong and prolonged phasic inhibition in M71 transgenic mitral cells, reminiscent of PGC-mediated feedforward inhibition.
source: Furthermore, mitral cell patch-clamp recordings reveal that acetophenone evokes strong and prolonged phasic inhibition in M71 transgenic mitral cells, reminiscent of PGC-mediated feedforward inhibition described previously (Fukunaga et al., 2014).
evidence: Summary of electrophysiology findings with citation to supporting literature.

claim: Feedforward inhibitory activity is likely to provide an effective mechanism to transform pervasive glomerular activity into sparse mitral cell responses.
source: This feedforward inhibitory activity is likely to provide an effective mechanism to transform pervasive glomerular activity into sparse mitral cell responses.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the functional role of feedforward inhibition.

claim: At high acetophenone concentrations, excitation may override inhibition, exposing the limits of olfactory bulb circuit mechanisms to normalize glomerular activity.
source: However, we found that increasing acetophenone concentration dramatically increased the fraction of responsive mitral cells, resulting in dense neural odor representations similar to the dense patterns of acetophenone-evoked glomerular activity. Thus, at high acetophenone concentrations, excitation may override inhibition, exposing the limits of olfactory bulb circuit mechanisms to normalize glomerular activity.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the breakdown of normalization at high stimulus intensities.

claim: Odorants commonly evoke phasic inhibition in wild-type mice.
source: Whole cell recordings of mitral cells reveal that odorants commonly evoke phasic inhibition in wild-type mice (as described previously e.g Fukunaga et al., 2014; Margrie et al., 2001)
evidence: Statement about odor-evoked inhibition in controls supported by citations.

claim: Inhibition in response to odorants other than acetophenone is significantly reduced in M71 transgenic mice.
source: and that this inhibition in response to odorants other than acetophenone is significantly reduced in M71 transgenic mice.
evidence: Summary of electrophysiology findings comparing inhibition between genotypes.

claim: Olfactory bulb inputs ordinarily evoke non-specific inhibition that can only be overcome by strong and specific input.
source: This result suggests that olfactory bulb inputs ordinarily evoke non-specific inhibition that can only be overcome by strong and specific input.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the role of inhibition in normal olfactory processing.

claim: In M71 transgenic mice, non-acetophenone inputs are too weak to recruit inhibition, allowing these weak inputs to evoke responses.
source: By contrast, in the M71 transgenic mice, non-acetophenone inputs are too weak to recruit inhibition, allowing these weak inputs to evoke responses.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion about the mechanism of signal amplification in M71 transgenic mice.

claim: Weak signals may be actively amplified by electrical coupling between mitral cells and self-excitation of intraglomerular mitral cell assemblies.
source: However, weak signals may also be actively amplified. For example, electrical coupling electrical coupling between mitral cells connected to the same glomerulus, and self-excitation of intraglomerular mitral cell assemblies, can further facilitate the detection of weak odor signals (Christie et al., 2005; Isaacson, 1999; Margrie et al., 2001; Murphy et al., 2005; Schoppa and Westbrook, 2001).
evidence: Discussion of potential amplification mechanisms with citations to supporting literature.

claim: A multi-synaptic pathway involving olfactory bulb tufted cells may directly amplify the output of mitral cells in response to weak inputs.
source: However, a multi-synaptic pathway involving olfactory bulb tufted cells may also directly amplify the output of mitral cells in response to weak inputs (De Saint Jan et al., 2009; Fukunaga et al., 2012; Gire et al., 2012; Najac et al., 2011).
evidence: Discussion of alternative amplification mechanism with citations to supporting literature.

claim: The patterns of mitral cell activity are more variable across multiple odorant presentations in M71 transgenic mice.
source: Interestingly, however, we observed that the patterns of mitral cell activity are more variable across multiple odorant presentations.
evidence: Summary of findings about trial-to-trial variability in M71 transgenic mice.

claim: The fraction of mitral cells responding reliably to the same stimulus is significantly reduced in M71 transgenic mice.
source: The fraction of mitral cells responding reliably to the same stimulus is significantly reduced in M71 transgenic mice, and the variation of the average fraction of responsive neurons for a given trial is increased.
evidence: Quantitative summary of response reliability findings.

claim: In M71 transgenic mice, the number of sensory neurons expressing a given odorant receptor are strongly reduced, limiting the power of averaging to reduce variability.
source: In M71 transgenic mice, the number of sensory neurons expressing a given odorant receptor are strongly reduced, thus limiting the power of averaging to reduce variability.
evidence: Interpretive explanation for increased variability based on reduced receptor convergence.

claim: Increased variability of neural odor representation will affect the accuracy of odor discrimination in M71 transgenic mice.
source: We speculate that this increased variability of a neural odor representation will affect the accuracy of odor discrimination in M71 transgenic mice, a model consistent with the olfactory discrimination deficits observed for difficult to discriminate odorant mixtures.
evidence: Speculative interpretation linking increased variability to behavioral deficits.

claim: Amplification of weak signals and suppression of strong, pervasive input patterns are likely to be crucial under normal circumstances.
source: In conclusion, we report a number of ways in which the olfactory bulb can modify substantially altered primary inputs to generate meaningful odor representations. Amplification of weak signals and suppression of strong, pervasive input patterns are likely to be crucial under normal circumstances, for example by allowing the system to tune to odors with considerable variations in vapor pressures.
evidence: Concluding statement about the general significance of the findings for normal olfactory function.

claim: Each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one of ~1300 odorant receptor genes in mice.
source: In mice, each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one of ~1300 odorant receptor genes, and each of these receptors interacts with multiple odorants (Chess et al., 1994; Malnic et al., 1999).
evidence: Statement about olfactory receptor expression supported by citations to foundational literature.

claim: Neurons expressing a given receptor are distributed randomly across large zones of the olfactory epithelium.
source: Neurons expressing a given receptor are distributed randomly across large zones of the olfactory epithelium, but project to two spatially invariant glomeruli in the olfactory bulb, the first processing center of olfactory information in the mammalian brain (Ressler et al., 1994; Vassar et al., 1994).
evidence: Statement about olfactory sensory neuron organization supported by citations.

claim: Mitral and tufted cells extend their apical dendrite into a single glomerulus.
source: The principal neurons of the olfactory bulb, mitral and tufted cells, extend their apical dendrite into a single glomerulus, and thus only receive direct input from sensory neurons expressing a single odorant receptor.
evidence: Statement about mitral cell anatomy based on established knowledge.

claim: Mitral cells tend to be narrowly tuned and only respond to a small number of odorants.
source: Electrophysiological and imaging experiments have revealed that, consistent with this anatomical organization, mitral cells tend to be narrowly tuned and only respond to a small number of odorants (Davison and Katz, 2007; Tan et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement about mitral cell tuning properties supported by citations.

claim: The spatiotemporal patterns of mitral cell firing are strongly shaped by the activity of local inhibitory neurons.
source: The spatiotemporal patterns of mitral cell firing are strongly shaped by the activity of local inhibitory neurons, including periglomerular cells, EPL interneurons, and granule cells (Banerjee et al., 2015; Fukunaga et al., 2014; Kato et al., 2013; Luo and Katz, 2001; Miyamichi et al., 2013; Yokoi et al., 1995).
evidence: Statement about the role of inhibition in shaping mitral cell activity supported by multiple citations.
